editorial:
Imagine moving to a tiny Russian town and instantly becoming the most hated kid in school. That is exactly what happens to twelve-year-old Lena. She is staying with her grandfather and just wants to fit in, but she finds herself caught in a messy situation with her classmates. A group of kids skips a literature class to go to the movies, and someone snitches. Because of this, the whole class loses their trip to Moscow. Lena takes the blame for the betrayal to protect a boy she really likes, and suddenly, she is a social outcast. You will feel for her as she deals with the mean comments and the lonely silence of being boycotted by everyone she knows.

What really makes this story work is how it captures that painful feeling of middle school drama. The acting is natural, and you can really feel Lena's struggle as she waits for the boy to do the right thing. It is a slow burn, but it hits hard emotionally. If you enjoy stories about growing up and learning tough lessons about loyalty, you will love this. You should definitely look for a high-quality 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection so you can see the beautiful old-school scenery, or just rent it on Apple TV for a cozy movie night at home.
endingExplained: The tension peaks when Lena can no longer handle the bullying and the guilt of the lie. The boy she protected finally sees how much she is suffering because of his cowardice. He eventually admits the truth to the class, clearing Lena's name. While the classmates apologize, the movie ends by showing that the emotional scars remain. It wraps up as a lesson on honesty and how true love means protecting someone's honor, not just their secrets.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves heartfelt stories about childhood and friendship.
